criteria.semantics: A native <ul> named by the list's label (aria-label), one native <li> per item.

keyboard.outcome: Passes it by: it is not a stop in the tab order.
Move to the list, and from item to item.

criteria.name: The list's label.
criteria.role: List, with its number of items.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my text size to 200% I SEE the items grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I zoom the page to 400% I SEE the items stack in one column, with no horizontal scrolling.

check.statement: The face emits a native <ul> element.
The list is named by its label in aria-label.
Every item is a native <li>, one per item of the list.
WHEN I reach the list with a desktop screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) I HEAR its name, the role of list and how many items it has.
WHEN I move through it I HEAR each item, and where the list ends.

criteria.semantics: The list's label, then each item after a bullet (•), in fg on bg; an item that is a link or a control is a stop in the tab order, the list itself is not. Once GPUI exposes a tree: an AccessKit List of ListItems, named by its label.

keyboard.outcome: Pass the list by: it is no stop of its own; the controls before and after it are.

keyboard.key: Tab (an item that is a link or control)
keyboard.outcome: Focus moves to the item, in reading order.

criteria.name: The list's label.
criteria.role: List, with its number of items.

setting.statement: WHEN I set the system text size to 200% (Windows' Accessibility, Text size; GNOME's Large Text or text scaling factor) I SEE the label and the items grow with it, with no loss of information.

WHEN I raise the display scale (macOS' Displays, Larger Text; Windows' Scale at 150% or 200%; GNOME's Scale at 200%) I SEE the label and the items drawn sharp and larger, whole and without overlapping.

WHEN I turn on the platform's high contrast (macOS' Increase contrast, a Windows contrast theme, the desktop portal's contrast) I SEE the window switch to the high-contrast palette by itself, the label and the items at 7:1.
WHEN I choose the high-contrast theme for the window I SEE the label and the items drawn in the high-contrast palette, every pair at 7:1.
WHEN I magnify the screen (macOS Zoom, Windows Magnifier, GNOME's Zoom) I SEE the label and the items whole and legible in the magnified view.

check.statement: A list adds no stop of its own to the window's tab order.
I SEE each item set apart by a bullet, not only by spacing.
WHEN I reach the list with VoiceOver (macOS), Narrator (Windows) or Orca (Linux) I HEAR its name and how many items it has, and each item in turn.

announce.api: AXList of AXGroup items, its label as the AXDescription (AccessKit Role::List, ListItem).
ControlType List of ListItems, its label as the Name.
ATSPI_ROLE_LIST of ATSPI_ROLE_LIST_ITEM, its label as the name.

criteria.note: GPUI 0.2.2 exposes no accessibility tree (no AccessKit, NSAccessibility, UI Automation or AT-SPI provider), so every HEAR check is blocked by the toolkit, and so are the system text size and the platform's high contrast, which it does not report. GPUI's main branch has AccessKit (zed-industries/zed#56065), not yet released (gpui/README.md, "Accessibility tree"). Its SEE checks with a probe run on GPUI's test platform (gpui/src/native.rs, every_gpui_see_check_with_a_probe_holds), which no CI job runs yet; the rest are reported as not verified.
